forecast-period.text: A high pressure system over SA continues to drift eastwards to be centred over the eastern states by Sunday. A low pressure system and associated trough move into the far west later Sunday and then moves across the state on Monday and out over the eastern states by later Tuesday. Another high moves into the west later Tuesday and over SA on Wednesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Early morning fog about the agricultural area, mainly on and east of the ranges. Showers and possible thunderstorms about the northwest, extending across the west during the day, tending to rain about the far northwest. Maximum temperatures below average, tending above average about the agricultural areas. Northeast to northwesterly winds, freshening in the west ahead of a southwest to southerly in the far southwest later.

Isolated light showers about southern coasts, clearing during the evening. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the far northwest. Southwest to southeasterly winds, tending east to northeasterly in the west.

Showers extending statewide, tending to rain about parts of the pastoral districts the West Coast and Eyre Peninsula, possibly extending into central districts in the evening. Possible thunderstorms about the pastoral districts, extending into northern Eyre Peninsula and the Flinders district. Maximum temperatures below average, remaining above average about the far northeast and southeast. Freshening north to northwesterly winds ahead of a fresh to strong and gusty southwest to southerly change extending from the west.

Showers about the agricultural area, and south of the pastoral districts, tending to rain about central and eastern parts of the agricultural area during the morning, contracting eastwards during the day. Possible thunderstorms about the northeast. Maximum temperatures generally below average. North to northwesterly winds ahead of a fresh southwest to southerly change about central parts, extending throughout during the morning then winds easing during the day.

text.p: Isolated showers about the agricultural area. Maximum temperatures generally below average, tending about average in the southwest. Southwest to southeasterly winds, tending northeast to northerly in the west.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Wednesday: Broadly 1 to 5 mm, increasing to 5 to 15 mm about the West Coast and North West pastoral districts and the agricultural areas, increasing further to 15 to 30 mm about parts of the west coast, Eyre Peninsula and central parts of the agricultural area. Isolated local falls of 30 to 60 mm are also possible in these areas and with thunderstorms.
